issue.body: Following https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/60828 report, an additional IT yml test has been added to verify the wildcard pattern data stream matching for EQL search.

body:
Backing datastream indices are also not matched
```javascript
// 1 result returned
GET .ds-logs-elastic.*/_search
  "query": """
    any where true
  """
  ,
  "size": 1
}
```

```javascript
// no results, no errors
GET .ds-logs-elastic.*/_eql/search
{
  "query": """
    any where true
  """
  ,
  "size": 1
}
```
Update: after a lot of tests local and remote on Cloud, the same build on both Cloud and local seem to work differently, as in locally the wildcard on data streams works, on Cloud they do not.

issue.title: Fix data stream wildcard resolution bug in eql search api.

labels.name: Team:Data Management (obsolete)
labels.description: DO NOT USE. This team no longer exists.

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
The eql search api redirects to the search api. For this reason the eql search api could work with concrete data stream names.
However if security is enabled and a data stream name snippet with a wildcard was used then it could not resolve this expressions.
This is because the EqlSearchRequest class didn't overwrite the `includeDataStreams()` method. This pr fixes this, so that
the security layer can properly expand data stream name wildcard expressions for the eql search api.

This commit also moves the eql data stream test to xpack rest tests, so that the test runs with security enabled.
This is required to reproduce the bug.

Closes #60828 

cc/ @astefan
